title: Architecture: In-App Messaging & Trade Chat — xCube
overview: The messaging feature adds a real-time channel-based chat layer to xCube. The architecture prioritises sub-500ms delivery latency, horizontal scalability to 10,000 concurrent connections, and a compliant 7-year message retention pipeline. The new Message Service sits alongside existing xCube backend services, reusing PostgreSQL (RDS) for channel metadata and adding Cassandra for message storage and Redis Pub/Sub for fan-out.
approach: Adds a new stateless Message Service alongside existing xCube backend services and a WebSocket gateway for real-time delivery, reusing the existing quote WebSocket infrastructure for ticker card price updates rather than building new market-data plumbing.

key_decisions.choice: Two-stage: in-process rule-based classifier (<5ms), then async LLM prompt-based classifier (~200ms)

new_entities.name: channels (PostgreSQL)
new_entities.key_fields: id UUID PK, name TEXT UNIQUE, topic TEXT, created_by UUID, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ, member_count INT

new_entities.name: channel_members (PostgreSQL)
new_entities.key_fields: channel_id UUID, user_id UUID, joined_at TIMESTAMPTZ
new_entities.relationships: N:1 with channels, N:1 with users

new_entities.name: messages (Cassandra)
new_entities.purpose: Message storage partitioned by channel, most-recent-first reads, 7-year TTL for compliance
new_entities.key_fields: channel_id UUID (partition key), created_at TIMESTAMP (clustering key desc), message_id UUID, user_id UUID, content TEXT, ticker_ref TEXT (JSON nullable), moderation_status TEXT (approved|pending|rejected)

repository_impact.changes_required: New channels and messages services; Cassandra client + schema migrations; Redis Pub/Sub fan-out; Moderation Service (rule-based + LLM classifier); WebSocket gateway integration; Archive pipeline (Debezium + Kafka producer)
repository_impact.notes: Message Service pods are stateless — scale independently from existing API pods

repository_impact.changes_required: New Chat tab in bottom nav; channel browser, channel detail with message thread; compose box with ticker card attachment; WebSocket manager for real-time messages; deep-link handler for ticker card tap
repository_impact.notes: Ticker card price updates via existing quote WebSocket; no new quote infrastructure on mobile

repository_impact.changes_required: New Chat tab; channel list fragment; message thread RecyclerView with DiffUtil; ticker card ViewHolder; WebSocket connection manager; deep-link handler
repository_impact.notes: Background message delivery via FCM for unread notifications (Phase 2); MVP is foreground-only

repository_impact.changes_required: New Cassandra cluster provisioning; Kafka topic: messages.archive; S3 bucket: xcube-message-archive with 7-year lifecycle policy; Athena table definition for compliance queries
repository_impact.notes: Separate from main RDS cluster; Cassandra on EC2 (3-node cluster) not Fargate

new_dependencies.name: Apache Cassandra
new_dependencies.not_solvable_with_existing_stack_because: PostgreSQL cannot sustain the projected 50K writes/sec at market open without severe contention on message rows; Cassandra's partition-key model aligns naturally with channel-scoped queries and provides native TTL for 7-year retention at scale.

new_dependencies.name: Debezium CDC + Kafka
new_dependencies.not_solvable_with_existing_stack_because: The compliance archive requirement demands zero-loss capture of every message written to Cassandra, including crash scenarios. Periodic batch export from the Message Service cannot guarantee completeness. Debezium CDC tails the Cassandra commit log; Kafka provides durable buffering before S3.

open_questions.decision: Cassandra cluster sizing for 3-year message volume at 10K MAU sending 10 messages/day
open_questions.recommendation: Model at 10B messages/year; r6g.xlarge × 3 handles ~50K writes/sec — sufficient. Review at 50K MAU milestone.
open_questions.risk: Under-provisioned cluster causes write failures at market open peak

open_questions.decision: LLM classifier model selection for moderation
open_questions.recommendation: Claude Haiku for cost-efficiency (~$0.0003/message); evaluate Mistral as fallback; do not use GPT-4 at MVP volumes due to cost
open_questions.risk: Model prompt injection via crafted message content — test adversarially before launch

open_questions.decision: Message hold vs. deliver-then-remove for flagged content
open_questions.recommendation: Hold before delivery for MVP (safer); accept latency cost for flagged messages; revisit if false-positive rate >5% creates UX complaints
open_questions.risk: Hold approach means legitimate messages may be delayed 10–30 minutes during human review queue backup
